answer: Trust propagates through an attestation graph by bounded random walks, limiting influence to paths reachable within the walk horizon. A sybil cluster may wander internally, but a sparse external cut gives it low conductance—the boundary weight relative to the smaller side’s volume—so few trusted paths enter. With capped edge weights, min-cut and transitivity bounds limit imported trust and thus aggregate voting weight; an ember-like clique cannot manufacture authority or claim an oasis of trust.
